<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2e710ba6a9e66751a4ecaaaf430f61ebaa72cc8d` — the merge of head `8f3bfc202c91986f94994dfc0974d842dea45603` into base `c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2e710ba6a9e66751a4ecaaaf430f61ebaa72cc8d && git checkout 2e710ba6a9e66751a4ecaaaf430f61ebaa72cc8d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138 8f3bfc202c91986f94994dfc0974d842dea45603 && git checkout -B drift-repro c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138 && git merge --no-ff 8f3bfc202c91986f94994dfc0974d842dea45603

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c32bb6ccbb293a4bda77010ce7ad416fcfeb1138
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cz4f7zEQZ2C9GTG382
Request: review · area E2b · head 8f3bfc20 · Fixes #32744

Area notes for the reviewer:
- Items 1 and 3 are pin only. Item 2's element check sits in the shared recogniser `packageScopedRefusalCandidates` (`@objectstack/types`), outside packages/rest: a rest-only check was measured to make the /data doors disagree on a malformed list. Please judge that placement.
- Declared `Clause-②: no`: a refusal whose candidates hold a non-holder element (no framework producer builds one) stops echoing `details.candidates`. Please judge `no` vs `no (narrowing)`.
- Folded #32761 (non-finite declared status) is measured, not fixed: it needs a TO decision and touches metadata-protocol (E1). It goes to a loose-ends card when this lands.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `8f3bfc202c91986f94994dfc0974d842dea45603`
Local-runs: none

Read: the PR's three commits on top of `main` (7 files, +234/−4): `packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts` and its test, `packages/rest/src/error-response.ts`, two rest suites, one rest doc comment and the changeset. I checked each claim against the code at this head and grepped every caller of the recogniser across `packages/`. CI was still running when I read it (22 success, 11 skipped, 30 in progress, 0 failed).

**(1) The check belongs in `@objectstack/types`. Accept the lease deviation.**
- `packageScopedRefusalCandidates` is the one recogniser, and four doors read it: `resolveThrownHttpError` (types), `mapDataError` (`packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts:1670`), the row error `toRowApiError` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-client-failures.ts:168`) and the rest wrapper (`packages/rest/src/error-response.ts:290-291`). No other call site exists outside tests.
- A check written only in rest guards one of those four exits. The report measured exactly that split: `createMany` withheld the list while the single `/data` doors and the row errors still echoed it. With the check inside the recogniser, every door gives one answer, and that is the property the recogniser's own doc promises ("so no door carries a second recogniser").
- Dropping the `as readonly PackageScopedHolder[]` cast in `error-response.ts:291` is a real gain. Before, the compiler checked nothing; now it checks that the types holder shape is assignable to core's. N1 names the direction it still does not check.

**(2) `Clause-②: no` is right. `no (narrowing)` is not.**
- *Public surface.* `packageScopedRefusalCandidates` is exported (`packages/types/src/index.ts:43`, `export *`). Its parameter is still `unknown`. Its return type narrows from `readonly unknown[] | undefined` to `readonly PackageScopedRefusalHolder[] | undefined` (`thrown-http-error.ts:232`). A narrower return type is covariant: every caller that compiled before still compiles. It is not an exported function whose accept set shrinks. The holder type alias (`thrown-http-error.ts:255`) and the guard (`:266`) are not exported, so no export, option or parameter is added.
- *Behaviour.* The only answer that moves is for a refusal whose `refusal.candidates` is an array with a non-holder element: before, the list; now, `undefined`. That is the answer the function already gave when `candidates` is not an array, so the answer set gains no new kind of value. On every wire door the status (409), the `code` (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`) and the sentence stay the same, and only `details.candidates` is withheld. Under the doctrine that is a refusal turning into another refusal, so `no`.
- *The moved input was never in the contract.* Core types the refusal's list as `readonly PackageScopedHolder[]` (`packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts:436`), with `PackageScopedHolder` at `:363-367`. The published wire member is typed `readonly PackageScopedHolder[]` in `@objectstack/client` (`packages/client/src/index.ts:806`, `package-address.ts:214-216`). The old echo of a non-holder broke that published type, and the new answer brings the doors back inside it.
- *Producer claim, verified.* Every `new PackageScopedNameRefusedError(...)` across `packages/` (about 40 sites: metadata, metadata-protocol, objectql, runtime, plugin-security, plugin-sharing, plugin-approvals, service-automation, service-analytics, rest analytics) builds its list typed `PackageScopedHolder[]`, so the compiler confirms every element is one of the four kinds. The security catalog's `candidates: ...map(describePackageScopedHolder)` (strings, `packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts:701,803,843,862`) is a `SecurityCatalogResolution`, not a thrown `refusal`. The only plain object with a `refusal` member and an HTTP status, `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts:209`, sets `refusal: true`, which the recogniser already rejects at `refusal.status !== 'refused'`. I found no framework producer that can build a non-holder element.
- *Why not `no (narrowing)`.* That form is for a narrowing that reaches no public contract. If this were a narrowing, it would reach an exported function, and the record would have to be `yes (narrowing)`, not `no (narrowing)`. It is not a narrowing: nothing a caller could write is newly refused, the parameter does not narrow, and the only input that moves already broke the published type of the member it fed. The remaining risk: a third-party plugin that throws a plain error of this shape with non-holder elements loses an echo the member's type never allowed. That is a bug-fix move, not an accept-set move.
- *Level.* `@objectstack/types: patch` and `@objectstack/rest: patch` are right for `Clause-②: no` with `Metadata-protocol: none`. No authorable metadata moves. `metadata-protocol` changes behaviour only through its `@objectstack/types` dependency, and the changesets dependency bump carries that; its source has no diff, so it needs no changeset entry of its own. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body (lines 6–7) and in the changeset. No `!`, BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.

**The pins measure what they claim.**
- `rest-batch-endpoint.test.ts`: the class thrown by a create op and by an update op, and a plain error of the class's shape, each answer `409` with `{ error, code, details: { candidates } }` checked with `toEqual`, so an extra or missing member fails the test. Each case asserts the throwing engine call was reached. All four holder kinds pass through, the five malformed lists each answer without `details`, and the CONTROL case (a `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with no refusal carries no details) is present. The report's ablation (5 failed of 32 rest cases, exactly the malformed lists; 1 of 16 types cases) shows the malformed-list cases measure the check.
- `package-door-declared-code.test.ts`: `POST /packages/publish` asserts the seam was called once, then the declared envelope, `409`, `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and `details` equal to `{ candidates }`.
- `thrown-http-error.test.ts`: the malformed lists are checked on the recogniser itself and on `resolveThrownHttpError`, `thrownAnswerOf` and `mapDataError`, with status and code held at 409 and `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`.

**Nits (none blocks).**
- N1. The holder shape is spelled out twice: core's `PackageScopedHolder` (`package-scoped-resolution.ts:363-367`) and the types alias (`thrown-http-error.ts:255-259`). Only one direction is compiler-checked: types' shape must be assignable to core's (`error-response.ts:291`). If core adds a fifth kind, everything still compiles, and every door then silently withholds `details.candidates` for a real refusal that names it. A type-level assertion in rest closes that gap, for example `const _coreHoldersPass: NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof sharedPackageScopedRefusalCandidates>>[number] = {} as PackageScopedHolder;`. The jsdoc at `error-response.ts:285-288` should then say the check runs both ways.
- N2. The changeset says the move happens on "a batch row's error". That door, `toRowApiError` (`protocol-client-failures.ts:168`), has no malformed-list pin at this head; the types and rest suites cover the other exits. One row-error case in metadata-protocol would pin it. If adding it is out of the lease, a loose-ends card is enough.
- N3. `packageScopedRefusalCandidates` is public, and its signature now names a type that callers cannot import (`PackageScopedRefusalHolder` is not exported). This is harmless, because `ReturnType<>` reaches it and `check:api-surface` records only that an export exists. Exporting it, or adding a jsdoc line saying it is core's `PackageScopedHolder`, would help a reader of the `.d.ts`.

Folded #32761 was measured and not fixed. Sending it to the loose-ends card at landing is right: its TO is a decision, and the fix reaches metadata-protocol (lease E1).
